meta.purpose: Reference bank + rules for generating correct camera-angle changes, shot scale transitions, and UGC-friendly shot lists.

meta.reliability_note: This is a prompt-engineering and creative reference dataset, not a legal credits database. Use title/year/source_basis for reference selection; verify exact credits before publishing production credits.

dop_and_editor_principles.meaning: A move must reveal action, information, emotion, power shift, POV or geography; otherwise keep the camera still.
A cut is correct when it preserves the emotional beat and story clarity; technical continuity supports, not replaces, the beat.
Place the next important object where the viewer's eye is already moving, or guide the eye through motion/sound/text.
Before close-ups or fast cuts, establish enough space for the viewer to understand relations and direction.
Prefer ELS→LS→MS→CU/insert or CU→MCU/MS→wide unless a deliberate contrast is motivated.
A focal-length change changes psychology and space; keep it consistent or assign it to a POV/emotional shift.
After product beauty, show behavior: face reaction, screen result, hands using it, pet response, or social proof.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut directly from a close-up or extreme close-up to an extreme long shot by default.
negative_rules.why: It tears the viewer away from emotional focus and resets geography too violently.
negative_rules.fix: Insert a medium/wide bridge, match action, sound bridge, reaction cutaway, or use the wide as a deliberate reveal.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut between two shots of the same subject from almost the same angle/size unless you want a jump cut.
negative_rules.why: Small perspective changes feel like an error, not a new idea.
negative_rules.fix: Move at least about 30 degrees, change lens/scale clearly, or cover with insert/B-roll.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cross the 180-degree line without a reset.
negative_rules.why: Screen direction and left/right relationships can flip, confusing the viewer.
negative_rules.fix: Use neutral-on-axis shot, motivated camera move across the line, cutaway, top shot, or new establishing shot.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not pan, orbit, gimbal-push or zoom only because the frame feels static.
negative_rules.why: Unmotivated movement looks cheap and distracts from story/product proof.
negative_rules.fix: Tie movement to new information, emotion, actor action, product reveal, or shift in power.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut to a reaction or object that violates the viewer's expected eyeline.
negative_rules.why: The viewer loses who is looking at what.
negative_rules.fix: Rebuild with POV → object → reaction, or use an insert that clarifies target.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not move the subject from left side to right side of frame across a cut without motivation.
negative_rules.why: The eye has to hunt for the subject and the edit feels clumsy.
negative_rules.fix: Match screen position, movement direction, gaze vector, or give a wider reset.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not mix handheld chaos, locked-off luxury, top-down tutorial and Dutch angle tension in the same short sequence without hierarchy.
negative_rules.why: The viewer reads it as lack of visual strategy.
negative_rules.fix: Pick a base grammar and allow one contrast grammar for the turning point.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut to a product/solution hero shot before the viewer understands the problem or desire.
negative_rules.fix: Set up problem → friction → discovery → proof → hero.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not start with a macro detail if the object is impossible to identify and mystery is not intended.
negative_rules.fix: Add an identifying insert within 1–2 beats or use audio/text to anchor.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not show only product shots for UGC claims; include human/pet reaction or proof context.
negative_rules.why: UGC needs trust and behavior, not just beauty frames.
negative_rules.fix: Add facecam, owner/pet interaction, screen proof, or side-by-side demo.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not use before/after transformations unless claims are safe, provable and not misleading.
negative_rules.why: Especially in beauty, health, pet and tech claims, false proof damages trust and can be non-compliant.
negative_rules.fix: Use demonstration, routine, testimonial framing, or measurable non-medical result.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut every phrase or every word in a testimonial/podcast scene.
negative_rules.why: It kills authenticity and removes micro-reactions.
negative_rules.fix: Cut on thought shifts, breaths, reactions, object inserts or laughter beats.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not cut between shots with conflicting key-light direction/time-of-day if the scene is meant to be continuous.
negative_rules.why: The viewer feels a continuity error even when they cannot name it.
negative_rules.fix: Use transitional B-roll, motivated location shift, or make the light change a story point.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not jump from ultra-wide distortion to compressed telephoto portrait without intent.
negative_rules.why: Space, face shape and product proportions change abruptly.
negative_rules.fix: Bridge with medium focal length or assign lens shift to POV change.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

negative_rules.rule: Do not use a wide establishing shot that contains no story tension, product context or mood information.
negative_rules.why: It slows the edit without helping orientation.
negative_rules.fix: Make the wide carry obstacle, scale, location value, before-state, or social proof.
negative_rules.allowed_exception: Only when it is an intentional stylistic device supported by story, sound, movement, or a clear reset.

mood_blocks.avoid: Over-stylized moves, shaky camera, fake urgency.
Showing product before problem is felt.
Too many overheads with no face/reaction.
Handheld chaos, jump cuts, cluttered backgrounds.
Studio-clean lighting that kills spontaneity.
Moving camera on every joke; comedy often needs a stable frame.
Mystery angles, unlabelled macro, inconsistent hand direction.
Unprovable before/after, medical claims, over-retouched skin.
Cutting off shoes/bag if the claim is full outfit.
Only product packshot; pet behavior is the proof.
Tiny unreadable screens, UI cuts without cursor/hand continuity.
Fast trend cuts that contradict the mood.
Dutch angles everywhere; instability needs contrast.
Anonymous claims with no human source.
Random handheld and cluttered props.
Speed without orientation; viewer must still know what changed.
Over-polished lighting that makes real testimony feel staged.
Hard smash cuts unless a mood break is intended.
Corporate symmetry and over-explaining.
Starting in CU and jumping to drone without narrative reason.
